name: mlb-data-2020-2025
title: MLB Data, 2007-2026
description: Major League Baseball data for all 30 clubs across the 2007-2026 seasons, scraped from Baseball-Reference and normalised into one tidy table per statistical category. Covers standard and advanced batting, pitching and fielding; value/WAR components; standings; schedules and results; rosters, coaching staffs and transactions; award voting; and game-level batting orders and defensive lineups.
rights: Data is sourced from Baseball-Reference.com, a Sports Reference LLC property, and remains their copyright. No open licence is granted or implied here. Credit Baseball-Reference.com as the source, and consult Sports Reference for any commercial or redistribution use.
citation: Baseball-Reference.com, Sports Reference LLC. MLB season data, 2020-2025. Retrieved 2026-10-01.
collectionMethod: Pages fetched over HTTP at a 3+ second crawl delay, honouring the Crawl-delay: 3 directive in the site robots.txt. Only /teams/, /leagues/ and /awards/ paths were requested. Tables embedded inside HTML comments were extracted along with the visible ones. Columns are keyed to Baseball-Reference data-stat codes, kept as sourceStatCode.
knownLimitations: 2020 was a 60-game COVID-shortened season; compare rates rather than counting stats.
2026 covers the regular season only; postseason and award voting stop at 2025.
The Athletics use franchise code OAK for 2020-2024 and ATH from 2025; same franchise.
Current_40_Man_Roster is a live snapshot marked Season 2026, not a historical series.
Player splits are disallowed by robots.txt and were not collected.
Statcast metrics are not published by Baseball-Reference and are not included.
regular_season files are team-scoped; advanced files are league-wide with 2TM/3TM rows. Do not union the two.
Rows where Row_Type is "summary" are table footers such as Team Totals, not players.

fields.name: PA
fields.description: Plate Appearances - When available, we use actual plate appearances from play-by-play game accounts - Otherwise estimated using AB + BB + HBP + SF + SH, - which excludes catcher interferences. - When this color click for a summary of each PA.

fields.name: Rbat
fields.description: Runs Batting - Number of runs better or worse than average the player was as a hitter. - This is based on a modified version of wRAA. - See our about section for a full description of how this is calculated.

fields.name: Rbaser
fields.description: Runs from Baserunning - Number of runs better or worse than average the player was for all baserunning events. - SB, CS, PB, WP, Defensive Indifference. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Rdp
fields.description: Runs Grounded into Double Plays - Number of runs better or worse than average the player was at avoiding grounding into double plays. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Rfield
fields.description: Runs from Fielding - Number of runs better or worse than average the player was for all fielding. - Fielding of balls in play, turning double plays, outfield arms and catcher defense are all included. - We use Baseball Info Solutions Defensive Runs Saved when available - (note that we do not use BIS catcher framing runs RszC ) and - Total Zone Rating from Sean Smith when not. - For Negro League seasons, we use Defensive Regression Analysis from Michael Humphreys. - Our WAR framework was developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Rpos
fields.description: Runs from Positional Scarcity - Number of runs above or below average due to positional differences. - Positions like C, SS, and 2B get a bonus. - Positions like 1B, DH, LF get a penalty. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: RAA
fields.description: Runs better than Avg - The number of runs this player is better than a league average player.

fields.name: WAA
fields.description: Wins Above Average for position players - A single number that presents the number of wins the player added - to the team above what a league average player would add. - Scale: 6+ MVP Quality, 3+ All-Star Quality, 0 Starter, - -2-0 Reserve, < -2 Replacement Level - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Rrep
fields.description: Runs from Replacement Level - Number of runs an average player is better than a replacement player. - Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. - Stronger leagues may get a larger bonus. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: RAR
fields.description: Runs Above Replacement Level - Total of other columns. The number of runs this player is better than a replacement player. Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: WAR
fields.description: Wins Above Replacement for position players - A single number that presents the number of wins the player added - to the team above what a replacement player (think AAA or AAAA) would add. - Scale: 8+ MVP Quality, 5+ All-Star Quality, 2+ Starter, - 0-2 Reserve, < 0 Replacement Level - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: waaWL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team in ONLY the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would only consider the games the pitcher threw in and ignoring games they did not play in.

fields.name: 162WL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team Season - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team for an entire season giving them credit for only the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would be waaW-L% - in the games the pitcher threw in and a .500 record otherwise.

fields.name: oWAR
fields.description: Offensive Wins Above Replacement (everything but Fielding) - The same statistic as Wins Above Replacement for Position - Players (WAR), but with the fielding value excluded. - oWAR + dWAR does not equal WAR. - Adding would count positions twice. - Contains the factor for batting stats, baserunning, a positional adjustment, and the replacement player adjustment. - Factors developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: dWAR
fields.description: Defensive Wins Above Replacement for position players - A defensive measure of wins above replacement, but given - only the defensive stats of the player and his position adjustment. For this calculation, we use a - replacement level on defense is the league average. - Based on Baseball Info Solutions defensive runs saved from 2003 on - and total zone rating developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com previously

fields.name: oRAR
fields.description: Offensive Runs above Replacement Level - oWAR + dWAR DOES NOT EQUAL WAR, pos would be counted 2x - Total of all columns except for fielding values - Includes batting, baserunning, positional adjustment, and a playing time adjustment - for the number of runs an average player is better than a replacement player. - Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Pos
fields.description: Positions Played - Positions are listed in order of games played at each. - * indicates the player appeared in at least 2/3rds of team games at that position (applies to a single season or a career total). - Positions after / indicate fewer than ten games played there. - 'H' indicates games as a pinch-hitter or pinch-runner.

fields.name: RA9
fields.description: Runs Allowed Per 9 IP - This is like ERA, but with unearned runs included.

fields.name: RA9opp
fields.description: Opponents’ Runs Scored Per 9 Inn - The average number of runs scored by this pitcher's opposition, per 9 innings. We use park factors to convert the opponent scoring to a league-average context.For in progress seasons, we consider the teams’ last 365 days. Interleague road games are excluded from the avg, and when the pitcher faces an interleague opp at home, we modify the opponent run scoring by .20 runs per 9inning depending on whether the DH is added or removed from their lineup. We assume a league average pitcher would allow this many runs.

fields.name: RA9def
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP of support from defense - This is based on the team’s Baseball Info Solutions Defensive Runs Saved since 2003 and Total Zone Rating before that. Negro League seasons use Defensive Regression Analysis. Positive values mean the team defense was above average. Negative means it was below average. We take the team’s total balls in play, the balls in play for this pitcher and the team’s total runs saved and split the runs among all of the team’s pitchers.

fields.name: RA9role
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP difference for SP and RP - From 1960 on we assess factor for starters and relievers. In that time, relievers have averaged a much lower ERA, and this factor accounts for that difference. Previously, this was part of our replacement level calculation, but it has now been moved into Runs Above Avg.

fields.name: PPFp
fields.description: Park Factor customized for parks the pitcher threw in - From 1908 on, we have full gamelogs, so we can say exactly how many innings a pitcher threw in each park. These are 3-year park factors weighted by batters faced in each park. Note the one-game park factor is the team PPF/100 minus 1 times two plus one, since the factors on team pages are for home and road games combined.

fields.name: RA9avg
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP for an avg pitcher - Equals PPFp/100*(oppRA9 - RAdef + RArole) - This is our best estimate of what an average pitcher would do against these opponents, with this defense and in these parks.

fields.name: RAA
fields.description: Runs better than Avg - IP*(RA9 avg - RA9)/9, then centered so the league average is always zero. - It is the number of runs this player is better than an average player. Adjusted for quality of opposition, parks pitched in and quality of team defense and recentered, so the league is zero.

fields.name: WAA
fields.description: Wins Above Average for pitchers - A single number that presents the number of wins the player added - to the team above what a league average player would add. - Scale: 6+ MVP Quality, 3+ All-Star Quality, 0 Starter, - -2-0 Reserve, < -2 Replacement Level - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: gmLI
fields.description: Game-entering Leverage Index - Solely for relief appearances, this is the average of each appearances opening leverage index - weighted by the batters faced in that outing. - The average pressure the pitcher or batter saw in this game or season. - 1.0 is average pressure, below 1.0 is low pressure and above 1.0 is high pressure.

fields.name: WAAadj
fields.description: Wins Above Avg Adjustment - For relief pitchers, we multiply WAA by (1+gmLI)/2. This is done in recognition of the added importance of high leverage. WAA adj is the additional value of this leverage adjustment. Also, the manner in which this and the WAA calculations are performed cause the league total WAA to move away from zero, so we also do an operation to recenter the entire league. The recentering forces the league sum to 0 which is as it should be for Wins Above Average. So for the league as a whole, WAA+WAA adj will equal zero and WAR = WAA + WAA adj + Replacement value

fields.name: WAR
fields.description: Wins Above Replacement for Pitchers - A single number that presents the number of wins the player added - to the team above what a replacement player (think AAA or AAAA) would add. This value includes defensive support and includes additional value for high leverage situations. - Scale: 8+ MVP Quality, 5+ All-Star Quality, 2+ Starter, - 0-2 Reserve, < 0 Replacement Level - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: RAR
fields.description: Runs better than Replacement Level - It is the number of runs this player is better than a replacement player. Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: waaWL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team in ONLY the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would only consider the games the pitcher threw in and ignoring games they did not play in.

fields.name: 162WL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team Season - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team for an entire season giving them credit for only the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would be waaW-L% - in the games the pitcher threw in and a .500 record otherwise.

fields.name: Awards
fields.description: Awards and honours for that season as listed by Baseball-Reference (e.g. AS = All-Star, MVP-1 = MVP winner).

fields.name: RA9extras
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP difference for pitching in extra innings - Starting in 2020, MLB had teams begin every extra inning with a runner on second base. If this runner scores, it is charged to the pitcher who started the inning. We adjust the pitcher's expected runs by the run expectancy that is added by the runner being placed on second base (approx 0.6 runs) for each time they start an extra inning.

fields.name: Oppo%

fields.name: RE24

fields.name: Hold

fields.description: Plate Appearances - When available, we use actual plate appearances from play-by-play game accounts - Otherwise estimated using AB + BB + HBP + SF + SH, - which excludes catcher interferences. - When this color click for a summary of each PA.

fields.name: Outs
fields.description: Outs Made - (At Bats - Hits) + Double Plays Grounded Into - + Sac. Flies + Sac. Hits + Caught Stealing.

fields.name: RC
fields.description: Runs Created - A set of formulas developed by Bill James and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s runs total. - This is computed with the "technical" formula when possible. - If SB or CS data is missing, the "basic" formula is used. - If HBP, IBB, SH, SF, or GIDP data is missing, the "stolen base" version of the formula is used. - Team Runs Created is the sum of player Runs Created.

fields.name: RC/G
fields.description: Runs Created per Game - Runs created per (approximately) 27 outs used. - Can be thought of as the runs produced by a lineup of 9 of this player.

fields.name: AIR
fields.description: Hitting AIR - measures the offensive level of the leagues and parks the - player played in relative to an all-time - average of a .335 OBP and .400 Slugging Percentage. Over 100 - indicates a favorable setting for hitters, under 100 a favorable - setting for pitchers.

fields.name: BAbip
fields.description: Batting Avg. on Balls in Plays (Hits - Home Runs)/(At Bats - SO - HR + Sac Flies) - This also measures how effectively the - defense turned balls into outs.

fields.name: BA
fields.description: Hits/At Bats - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played - Bold indicates either highest BA using current stats - or awarded title at end of year.

fields.name: lgBA
fields.description: League Batting Average - The batting average a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: OBP
fields.description: (H + BB + HBP)/(At Bats + BB + HBP + SF) - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: lgOBP
fields.description: League On-base Percentage - The on-base percentage a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: SLG
fields.description: Total Bases/At Bats or - (1B + 2*2B + 3*3B + 4*HR)/AB - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: lgSLG
fields.description: League Slugging Percentage - The slugging percentage a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: OPS
fields.description: On-Base + Slugging Percentages - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: lgOPS
fields.description: League On-Base + Slugging - The OPS a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: OPS+
fields.description: OPS+ - 100*[OBP/lg OBP + SLG/lg SLG - 1] - Adjusted to the player’s ballpark(s)

fields.name: OWn%
fields.description: Offensive Winning Percentage - The percentage of games a team with nine of this player - batting would win. Assumes average pitching and defense. - This uses the Pythagorean win pct formula with the player's RC/G for runs scored and the league's R/9 as runs allowed.

fields.name: BtRuns
fields.description: Adjusted Batting Runs - A set of formulas developed by Gary Gillette, Pete Palmer and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s runs total via linear weights. - 0.0 is an avg performance, <0 is worse than avg and >0 is better than avg

fields.name: BtWins
fields.description: Adjusted Batting Wins - A set of formulas developed by Gary Gillette, Pete Palmer and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s wins with his bat. - 0.0 is an avg performance, <0 is worse than avg and >0 is better than avg

fields.name: TotA
fields.description: Total Average - Developed by Thomas Boswell of the Washington Post - (Total Bases + HBP + BB + SB) / (AB - H + CS + GIDP)

fields.name: SecA
fields.description: Secondary Average - (Total Bases - Hits + BB + SB - CS) / AB - Over .500, excellent; < 200, poor

fields.name: ISO
fields.description: (Total Bases - H)/At Bats or - (2B + 2*3B + 3*HR)/AB - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: PwrSpd
fields.description: Power/Speed Number - 2 x (Home Runs x Stolen Bases)/(Stolen Bases + Home Runs) - The harmonic mean of HR and SB. - To do well you need a lot of both. - Developed by Bill James.

fields.name: Pos Summary
fields.description: Positions Played - The positions either followed by the games played at that position - or in order of games or innings played. - For a single season, * indicates they played at least 2/3rds of the team games there. - Positions after / indicate less than ten games played at those positions. - For career, a + sign means more than 300 games at that position and - a - sign means less than 30 games. - 'H' indicates games as a pinch-hitter or pinch-runner.

fields.description: Rbat+ - Batting runs as computed for WAR, but indexed to the environment the player played in, where 100 is league average.

fields.name: BAbip
fields.description: Batting Avg. on Balls in Plays (Hits - Home Runs)/(At Bats - SO - HR + Sac Flies) - This also measures how effectively the - defense turned balls into outs.

fields.name: ISO
fields.description: (Total Bases - H)/At Bats or - (2B + 2*3B + 3*HR)/AB - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: HR%
fields.description: Home Run Percentage - Percentage of all plate appearances a home run was hit. - (HR)/(all plate appearances)

fields.name: SO%
fields.description: Strikeout Percentage - Percentage of all plate appearances ending with a Strikeout. - (SO)/(all plate appearances)

fields.name: BB%
fields.description: Base on Balls Percentage - Percentage of all plate appearances ending with a Base on Balls. - (BB)/(all plate appearances)

fields.name: LD%
fields.description: Line Drive Percentage - Percentage of all balls put into play (including home runs) that are line drives. - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: GB%
fields.description: Ground Ball Percentage - Percentage of all balls put into play (including home runs) that are ground balls. - EXCLUDES Bunts - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: FB%
fields.description: Fly Ball Percentage - Percentage of all balls put into play (including home runs) that are fly balls. - EXCLUDES Popups - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: GB/FB
fields.description: Ground Ball to Fly Ball Ratio - Includes line drives as fly balls. - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: Pull%
fields.description: Pull Percentage - Percentage of all balls put into play (including home runs) that are hit to the batter's pull side. - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: Cent%
fields.description: Center Percentage - Percentage of all balls put into play (including home runs) that are hit to the center of the field. - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: Oppo%
fields.description: Opposite-Field Percentage - Percentage of all balls put into play (including home runs) that are hit to the batter's opposite (push) side. - Batted ball type and location is not complete prior to 1988.

fields.name: WPA
fields.description: Win Probability Added for Offensive Player - Given average teams, this is the change in probability - caused by this batter during the game. - See Win Expectancy explainer for details.

fields.name: cWPA
fields.description: Championship Win Probability Added for Offensive Player - Given average teams, this is the change in probability of winning the World Series, displayed in percentage points. - See Win Expectancy explainer for details.

fields.name: RE24
fields.description: Base-Out Runs Added - Given the bases occupied/out situation, how many runs did the batter - or baserunner add in the resulting play. - Compared to average, so 0 is average, and above 0 is better than average

fields.name: RS%
fields.description: Run Scoring Percentage - Percentage of times a baserunner eventually scores a run. - (R - HR) / (H + HBP + BB - HR + G_pr)

fields.name: SB%
fields.description: Stolen Base Percentage - SB / (SB + CS)

fields.name: XBT%
fields.description: Extra Bases Taken Percentage - Percentage of times the runner advanced more than one base on a single or more than two bases on a double, when possible. - Does not take into account the location or type of the ball in play.

fields.name: EV
fields.description: Average Exit Velocity - Average speed of the ball off the bat for balls put into play, measured in miles per hour.

fields.name: HardH%
fields.description: Hard Hit Rate - Percent of balls in play with an exit velocity of 95 mph or more.

fields.name: SVSit
fields.description: Save Situations - Pitcher entered the game after the fifth inning in a save situation. - Or pitcher entered earlier in the game and did not get the win. - When the starter did not go five innings, it is - possible to enter in a save situation and get the win. - Save Situation Defn. (any of three): - 1. team has a lead of no more - than three runs and and at least three outs remaining. - 2. The tying run is either on base, at bat or on deck. - 3. At three innings remain in the game. - For our purposes, a save situation is only one - of the first two.

fields.name: Hold
fields.description: Holds - Pitcher entered the game in a save situation and did not get - the win (due to < 5 IP by starter) or save. - The pitcher then retires at least one batter and leaves the game - without having relinquished the lead at any point. - A pitcher can get a hold and a loss, but not a hold and a win - or a hold and a save.

fields.description: American League or National League.

fields.description: East, Central or West.

fields.name: Division_Full
fields.description: League and division combined, e.g. "AL East".

fields.name: Tm
fields.description: Team as listed in the source table.

fields.name: R/G
fields.description: Runs Scored Per Game

fields.name: Outs
fields.description: Outs Made - (At Bats - Hits) + Double Plays Grounded Into - + Sac. Flies + Sac. Hits + Caught Stealing.

fields.name: RC
fields.description: Runs Created - A set of formulas developed by Bill James and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s runs total. - This is computed with the "technical" formula when possible. - If SB or CS data is missing, the "basic" formula is used. - If HBP, IBB, SH, SF, or GIDP data is missing, the "stolen base" version of the formula is used. - Team Runs Created is the sum of player Runs Created.

fields.name: RC/G
fields.description: Runs Created per Game - Runs created per (approximately) 27 outs used. - Can be thought of as the runs produced by a lineup of 9 of this player.

fields.name: AIR
fields.description: Hitting AIR - measures the offensive level of the leagues and parks the - player played in relative to an all-time - average of a .335 OBP and .400 Slugging Percentage. Over 100 - indicates a favorable setting for hitters, under 100 a favorable - setting for pitchers.

fields.name: BAbip
fields.description: Batting Avg. on Balls in Plays (Hits - Home Runs)/(At Bats - SO - HR + Sac Flies) - This also measures how effectively the - defense turned balls into outs.

fields.name: BA
fields.description: Hits/At Bats - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played - Bold indicates either highest BA using current stats - or awarded title at end of year.

fields.name: lgBA
fields.description: League Batting Average - The batting average a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: OBP
fields.description: (H + BB + HBP)/(At Bats + BB + HBP + SF) - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: lgOBP
fields.description: League On-base Percentage - The on-base percentage a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: SLG
fields.description: Total Bases/At Bats or - (1B + 2*2B + 3*3B + 4*HR)/AB - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: lgSLG
fields.description: League Slugging Percentage - The slugging percentage a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: OPS
fields.description: On-Base + Slugging Percentages - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: lgOPS
fields.description: League On-Base + Slugging - The OPS a league average - (non-pitcher) would have had in the same park(s).

fields.name: OPS+
fields.description: OPS+ - 100*[OBP/lg OBP + SLG/lg SLG - 1] - Adjusted to the player’s ballpark(s)

fields.name: OWn%
fields.description: Offensive Winning Percentage - The percentage of games a team with nine of this player - batting would win. Assumes average pitching and defense. - This uses the Pythagorean win pct formula with the player's RC/G for runs scored and the league's R/9 as runs allowed.

fields.name: BtRuns
fields.description: Adjusted Batting Runs - A set of formulas developed by Gary Gillette, Pete Palmer and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s runs total via linear weights. - 0.0 is an avg performance, <0 is worse than avg and >0 is better than avg

fields.name: BtWins
fields.description: Adjusted Batting Wins - A set of formulas developed by Gary Gillette, Pete Palmer and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s wins with his bat. - 0.0 is an avg performance, <0 is worse than avg and >0 is better than avg

fields.name: TotA
fields.description: Total Average - Developed by Thomas Boswell of the Washington Post - (Total Bases + HBP + BB + SB) / (AB - H + CS + GIDP)

fields.name: SecA
fields.description: Secondary Average - (Total Bases - Hits + BB + SB - CS) / AB - Over .500, excellent; < 200, poor

fields.name: ISO
fields.description: (Total Bases - H)/At Bats or - (2B + 2*3B + 3*HR)/AB - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: PwrSpd
fields.description: Power/Speed Number - 2 x (Home Runs x Stolen Bases)/(Stolen Bases + Home Runs) - The harmonic mean of HR and SB. - To do well you need a lot of both. - Developed by Bill James.

resources.description: Advanced and situational splits plus team- and league-level advanced aggregates, sourced from league pages so they cover every player in the majors.

fields.name: Season
fields.description: Season year, 2007-2026. On Current_40_Man_Roster it marks the date the snapshot was taken rather than a season that was played.

fields.name: Team
fields.description: Baseball-Reference franchise code (e.g. NYY). The Athletics are OAK through 2024 and ATH from 2025. 2TM/3TM marks a combined line for a player who changed clubs.

fields.name: Team_Name
fields.description: Full club name as of that season.

fields.name: League
fields.description: AL or NL.

fields.name: League_Name
fields.description: American League or National League.

fields.name: Division
fields.description: East, Central or West.

fields.name: Division_Full
fields.description: League and division combined, e.g. "AL East".

fields.name: Tm
fields.description: Team as listed in the source table.

fields.name: R/G
fields.description: Runs Scored Per Game

fields.name: BtRuns
fields.description: Adjusted Batting Runs - A set of formulas developed by Gary Gillette, Pete Palmer and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s runs total via linear weights. - 0.0 is an avg performance, <0 is worse than avg and >0 is better than avg

fields.name: BtWins
fields.description: Adjusted Batting Wins - A set of formulas developed by Gary Gillette, Pete Palmer and others - that estimates a player’s total contributions - to a team’s wins with his bat. - 0.0 is an avg performance, <0 is worse than avg and >0 is better than avg

fields.name: Plays
fields.description: Plays included in WPA calculations - For batters, this includes all batting plays and baserunning plays where they were the lead baserunner whose state changed.

fields.name: WPA
fields.description: Win Probability Added for Offensive Player - Given average teams, this is the change in probability - caused by this batter during the game. - See Win Expectancy explainer for details.

fields.name: WPA+
fields.description: Win Probability Added - Sum of positive events for this batter.

fields.name: WPA-
fields.description: Win Probability Subtracted - Sum of negative events for this batter.

fields.name: aLI
fields.description: Average Leverage Index - The average pressure the pitcher or batter saw in this game or season. - 1.0 is average pressure, below 1.0 is low pressure and above 1.0 is high pressure.

fields.name: WPA/LI
fields.description: Situational Wins (WPA/LI) - It is the sum of WPA divided by the leverage index for each play. - WPA depends greatly on the context of the at bats. - This stat does not.

fields.name: Clutch
fields.description: WPA Clutch - WPA (overall)/aLI - WPA/LI (as shown) - The difference between context dependent WPA and the context-neutral WPA.

fields.name: cWPA
fields.description: Championship Win Probability Added for Offensive Player - Given average teams, this is the change in probability of winning the World Series, displayed in percentage points. - See Win Expectancy explainer for details.

fields.name: cWPA+
fields.description: Championship Win Probability Added - Sum of positive events for this batter. - Displayed in percentage points.

fields.name: cWPA-
fields.description: Championship Win Probability Subtracted - Sum of negative events for this batter. - Displayed in percentage points.

fields.name: acLI
fields.description: Average Championship Leverage Index - The average pressure the pitcher or batter saw in this game or season. - 1.0 is average pressure, below 1.0 is low pressure and above 1.0 is high pressure.

fields.name: cClutch
fields.description: cWPA Clutch - cWPA (overall)/acLI - cWPA/cLI (as shown) - The difference between context dependent cWPA and the context-neutral cWPA. - Displayed in percentage points.

fields.name: RE24
fields.description: Base-Out Runs Added - Given the bases occupied/out situation, how many runs did the batter - or baserunner add in the resulting play. - Compared to average, so 0 is average, and above 0 is better than average

fields.name: REW
fields.description: Base-Out Wins Added (REW) - This is the number of wins above average the player was worth by their performance measured by the 24 - base-out situations across every play in the game.

fields.name: boLI
fields.description: Base-Out Leverage - The average base-out leverage seen across all plays.

fields.name: RE24/boLI
fields.description: Situational Runs - The summation of for each play the change in run-expectancy divided by the base-out leverage

fields.name: PHlev
fields.description: Pinch Hit Leverage Index - The importance of the context in which the Pinch Hitter was used - Above one means higher than average pressure. - Below one means lower than average pressure.

fields.name: AB
fields.description: Pinch Hit At Bats

fields.name: Row_Type
fields.description: 'data' for player rows; 'summary' for footer rows such as Team Totals.

fields.name: OBP
fields.description: (H + BB + HBP)/(At Bats + BB + HBP + SF) - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: SLG
fields.description: Total Bases/At Bats or - (1B + 2*2B + 3*3B + 4*HR)/AB - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: OPS
fields.description: On-Base + Slugging Percentages - For recent years, leaders need 3.1 PA - per team game played

fields.name: OPS+
fields.description: OPS+ - 100*[OBP/lg OBP + SLG/lg SLG - 1] - Adjusted to the player’s ballpark(s)

fields.name: TB
fields.description: Total Bases - Singles + 2 x Doubles + 3 x Triples + 4 x Home Runs.

fields.name: GDP
fields.description: Double Plays Grounded Into - Only includes standard 6-4-3, 4-3, etc. double plays. - First tracked in 1933. - For gamelogs only in seasons we have play-by-play, we include triple plays as well. - All official seasonal totals do not include GITP's.

fields.description: Runs from Fielding - Number of runs better or worse than average the player was for all fielding. - Fielding of balls in play, turning double plays, outfield arms and catcher defense are all included. - We use Baseball Info Solutions Defensive Runs Saved when available - (note that we do not use BIS catcher framing runs RszC ) and - Total Zone Rating from Sean Smith when not. - For Negro League seasons, we use Defensive Regression Analysis from Michael Humphreys. - Our WAR framework was developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Rpos
fields.description: Runs from Positional Scarcity - Number of runs above or below average due to positional differences. - Positions like C, SS, and 2B get a bonus. - Positions like 1B, DH, LF get a penalty. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: RAA
fields.description: Runs better than Avg - It is the number of runs this player is better than a league average player.

fields.name: WAA
fields.description: Wins Above Avg - This is the wins added by this player above that of an average player. We compute the waaW-L% using a PythagenPat conversion and then subtract .500 and multiply by the number of games played.

fields.name: Rrep
fields.description: Runs from Replacement Level - Number of runs an average player is better than a replacement player. - Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. - Stronger leagues may get a larger bonus. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: RAR
fields.description: Runs above Replacement Level - Total of other columns It is the number of runs this player is better than a replacement player. Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: WAR
fields.description: Wins Above Replacement - A single number that presents the number of wins the player added - to the team above what a replacement player (think AAA or AAAA) would add. - Scale for a single-season: 8+ MVP Quality, 5+ All-Star Quality, 2+ Starter, - 0-2 Reserve, < 0 Replacement Level - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: waaWL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team in ONLY the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would only consider the games the pitcher threw in and ignoring games they did not play in.

fields.name: 162WL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team Season - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team for an entire season giving them credit for only the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would be waaW-L% - in the games the pitcher threw in and a .500 record otherwise.

fields.name: oWAR
fields.description: Offensive Wins Above Replacement (everything but Fielding) - The same statistic as Wins Above Replacement for Position - Players (WAR), but with the fielding value excluded. - oWAR + dWAR does not equal WAR. - Adding would count positions twice. - Contains the factor for batting stats, baserunning, a positional adjustment, and the replacement player adjustment. - Factors developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: dWAR
fields.description: Defensive Wins Above Replacement for position players - A defensive measure of wins above replacement, but given - only the defensive stats of the player and his position adjustment. For this calculation, we use a - replacement level on defense is the league average. - Based on Baseball Info Solutions defensive runs saved from 2003 on - and total zone rating developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com previously

fields.name: oRAR
fields.description: Offensive Runs above Replacement Level - oWAR + dWAR DOES NOT EQUAL WAR, pos would be counted 2x - Total of all columns except for fielding values - Includes batting, baserunning, positional adjustment, and a playing time adjustment - for the number of runs an average player is better than a replacement player. - Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: Salary
fields.description: These values may not include every bonus the player received in a season. - They are also often missing values for mid-season callups or players acquired in-season. - Post-1984 seasons are mostly complete, pre-1985 is mostly incomplete.

fields.name: RA9
fields.description: Runs Allowed Per 9 IP - This is like ERA, but with unearned runs included.

fields.name: RA9opp
fields.description: Opponents’ Runs Scored Per 9 Inn - The average number of runs scored by this pitcher's opposition, per 9 innings. We use park factors to convert the opponent scoring to a league-average context.For in progress seasons, we consider the teams’ last 365 days. Interleague road games are excluded from the avg, and when the pitcher faces an interleague opp at home, we modify the opponent run scoring by .20 runs per 9inning depending on whether the DH is added or removed from their lineup. We assume a league average pitcher would allow this many runs.

fields.name: RA9def
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP of support from defense - This is based on the team’s Baseball Info Solutions Defensive Runs Saved since 2003 and Total Zone Rating before that. Negro League seasons use Defensive Regression Analysis. Positive values mean the team defense was above average. Negative means it was below average. We take the team’s total balls in play, the balls in play for this pitcher and the team’s total runs saved and split the runs among all of the team’s pitchers.

fields.name: RA9role
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP difference for SP and RP - From 1960 on we assess factor for starters and relievers. In that time, relievers have averaged a much lower ERA, and this factor accounts for that difference. Previously, this was part of our replacement level calculation, but it has now been moved into Runs Above Avg.

fields.name: PPFp
fields.description: Park Factor customized for parks the pitcher threw in - From 1908 on, we have full gamelogs, so we can say exactly how many innings a pitcher threw in each park. These are 3-year park factors weighted by batters faced in each park. Note the one-game park factor is the team PPF/100 minus 1 times two plus one, since the factors on team pages are for home and road games combined.

fields.name: RA9avg
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP for an avg pitcher - Equals PPFp/100*(oppRA9 - RAdef + RArole) - This is our best estimate of what an average pitcher would do against these opponents, with this defense and in these parks.

fields.name: RAA
fields.description: Runs better than Avg - IP*(RA9 avg - RA9)/9, then centered so the league average is always zero. - It is the number of runs this player is better than an average player. Adjusted for quality of opposition, parks pitched in and quality of team defense and recentered, so the league is zero.

fields.name: WAA
fields.description: Wins Above Avg - This is the wins added by this player above that of an average player. We compute the waaW-L% using a PythagenPat conversion and then subtract .500 and multiply by the number of games played.

fields.name: gmLI
fields.description: game-entering Leverage Index - Solely for relief appearances, this is the average of each appearances opening leverage index - weighted by the batters faced in that outing. - The average pressure the pitcher or batter saw in this game or season. - 1.0 is average pressure, below 1.0 is low pressure and above 1.0 is high pressure.

fields.name: WAAadj
fields.description: Wins Above Avg Adjustment - For relief pitchers, we multiply WAA by (1+gmLI)/2. This is done in recognition of the added importance of high leverage. WAA adj is the additional value of this leverage adjustment. Also, the manner in which this and the WAA calculations are performed cause the league total WAA to move away from zero, so we also do an operation to recenter the entire league. The recentering forces the league sum to 0 which is as it should be for Wins Above Average. So for the league as a whole, WAA+WAA adj will equal zero and WAR = WAA + WAA adj + Replacement value

fields.name: WAR
fields.description: Wins Above Replacement for Pitchers - A single number that presents the number of wins the player added - to the team above what a replacement player (think AAA or AAAA) would add. This value includes defensive support and includes additional value for high leverage situations. - Scale: 8+ MVP Quality, 5+ All-Star Quality, 2+ Starter, - 0-2 Reserve, < 0 Replacement Level - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: RAR
fields.description: Runs better than Replacement Level - It is the number of runs this player is better than a replacement player. Replacement is set for a .294 team winning percentage. - Developed by Sean Smith of BaseballProjection.com

fields.name: waaWL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team in ONLY the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would only consider the games the pitcher threw in and ignoring games they did not play in.

fields.name: 162WL%
fields.description: Win-Loss% w/ Avg. Team Season - This is the win-loss of an otherwise average team for an entire season giving them credit for only the games this player played in. - For example, for a pitcher this would be waaW-L% - in the games the pitcher threw in and a .500 record otherwise.

fields.name: Salary
fields.description: These values may not include every bonus the player received in a season. - They are also often missing values for mid-season callups or players acquired in-season. - Post-1984 seasons are mostly complete, pre-1985 is mostly incomplete.

fields.name: RA9extras
fields.description: Runs per 9 IP difference for pitching in extra innings - Starting in 2020, MLB had teams begin every extra inning with a runner on second base. If this runner scores, it is charged to the pitcher who started the inning. We adjust the pitcher's expected runs by the run expectancy that is added by the runner being placed on second base (approx 0.6 runs) for each time they start an extra inning.
